fatal_errors: Fails to identify the relevant material, the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with FCC and B2 phases.
Attributes the transition to conventional grain-boundary impurity segregation and precipitation, contrary to the target mechanism involving enhanced L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Omits the critical aging conditions near 600°C for embrittlement and 750°C for ductility recovery.
Provides no cited evidence supporting the proposed conventional-alloy explanation.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes only the generic possibility of a temperature-dependent ductile–brittle–ductile response. It does not answer which material exhibits the newly reported behavior and instead reverts to the conventional temper-embrittlement framework that the context contrasts against. The target is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA aged within roughly 550–750°C. Maximum embrittlement at about 600°C arises from strengthened L12 ordering, restricted cross-slip and planar slip, together with stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips. Recovery near 750°C follows reduced ordering and formation of ductile transition zones. The suggested experiment is generic and does not discriminate phase-boundary-tip crack initiation from grain-boundary segregation.
